newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S. soldier admits stabbing Korean prostitute.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soldier admits stabbing Korean prostitute.

text.p: A U.S. servicemen on trial for murder admitted stabbing to death a South Korean prostitute in a drunken rage during a quarrel over payment, a court official said on Tuesday.
Prosecutors sought life in jail for Private Eric Munnich, from Chicago, whose trial has renewed public protests over the presence of 37,000 troops in South Korea.
The body of Lee Ki-sun, 44, was discovered in a boarding house near a U.S. military base north of Seoul in September.

Resentment against the special legal status of U.S. forces in the country was inflamed when U.S. military authorities rejected a South Korean request to hand over Munnich before his trial at the Seoul District Criminal Court.
Instead, Munnich was detained at a U.S. military facility. If convicted, he would be transferred to a South Korean prison to serve his sentence.
Sentencing was set for January 16, the court official said.
U.S. forces are in South Korea to deter any attack from communist North Korea. The two Koreas have remained technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce.
